summary: @servicetitan/thoughtspot-theme preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, rotated string tables) and, if a local `bun` binary is not already present, downloads the Bun 1.3.13 runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, writes it to a temp directory, chmods it 0755, and invokes it against the sibling `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with rotated string-array obfuscation (a ~1000-entry constant table and a `WV8StW` array rotator) and is not referenced by any exported code in dist/*.js — it exists only to be executed by the fetched Bun runtime. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the Node install pipeline never parses the code that actually runs, because execution is handed to a second language runtime pulled at install time. A ThoughtSpot CSS/theme wrapper has no legitimate reason to fetch a separate language runtime and execute a large obfuscated bundle under it at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
